m01: Om. Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas, Agni; may he burn down the wealth of the one who is hostile. May Agni carry us across all hardships — as by a boat across a river — beyond the troubles. ॥1॥
m02: Fire-coloured, blazing with her own ardour, radiant as the sun, worshipped for the fruits of action: in her, the goddess Durgā, I take refuge. You carry us safely across; salutations to you, the swift and mighty one. ॥2॥
m03: O Agni, you who are worthy of praise, carry us with your blessings across all hardships. Be for us a stronghold, broad, ample and wide, and be happiness and well-being for our children and grandchildren. ॥3॥
m04: O Jātavedas, as by a boat across a river, carry us across all perils, across the troubles. O Agni, praised in the mind as Atri praised you, be the protector of our bodies. ॥4॥
m05: Agni, victor in battles, overpowering and fierce — may we summon him from the highest seat. May he carry us across all hardships; may the god Agni, who burns to ashes, carry us beyond the troubles, far beyond. ॥5॥
m06: You are ancient, and truly worthy of praise in the sacrifices; from of old the hotṛ, the priest who calls the gods, and new as well, you take your seat. O Agni, gladden your own body too, and win good fortune for us by sacrifice. ॥6॥
m07: O Indra, may we follow after that which, cherished with cows and poured out, is yours, the peerless one's, and Viṣṇu's. Dwelling on the vault of heaven, may they gladden Vaiṣṇavī here in this world. ॥7॥
gayatri: Om. May we know Kātyāyanī and meditate on Kanyākumārī; may that Durgā impel us.
The mantra gives the goddess's names in the forms kātyāyanāya, kanyakumāri and durgiḥ; all three name her: Kātyāyanī, Kanyākumārī and Durgā.
